                    ### Question
                    A 28-year-old man is brought to the emergency department by ambulance after being hit in the head with a baseball bat. Physical examination shows swelling and bruising around the left temple and eye. A CT scan of the head shows a transverse fracture through the sphenoid bone and blood in the sphenoid sinus. Neurological examination is most likely to show which of the following findings?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Left homonymous hemianopia
opb. Inward deviation of the left eye
opc. Left facial paralysis
opd. Decreased hearing in the left ear
ope. Deviation of uvula to the right

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The trauma to the head resulting in a transverse fracture through the sphenoid bone and blood in the sphenoid sinus can lead to cranial nerve compression and possible cranial nerve injury. This can manifest as neurological examination findings such as left facial paralysis, making option opc the most likely finding in this case.
